```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

**Status: EXPLORATORY and non-causal.** Fava biomass is not randomized. It is an *outcome* of the
pot's wheat inoculation (and of water), so here it is used the way root hyphal colonization is used
in the AMF figures: as a measured covariate whose relationship with wheat performance we want to
describe. Nothing here is in the confirmatory set, and every p-value is unadjusted for multiplicity.

**Data.** Intercrop pots only (`Poly == "Inter"`, n = 30: 5 per Inoc x Water cell). Monoculture pots
have no fava. Everything is **per pot**:

* `Fava_g` - biomass of the single fava plant in the pot (x-axis).
* `berry_alloc` - wheat berries / wheat total biomass. Wheat-only, so fava is not in the denominator.
* `W_NPP` - total biomass of the 6 wheat plants in the pot, in grams. (`Pot_NPP_g` is not used: it
  includes fava and would correlate with the x-axis by construction.)

**Models.** Beta regression (logit link) for allocation; `lm` on `log(W_NPP)` for biomass. Each
set of slopes comes from a single model fitted once, with slopes extracted by `emtrends`; no
subset models. Slopes are on the logit scale (allocation) or the log scale (biomass, so a slope
of 0.1 is about +10% per gram of fava). For each slope there are two p-values:

* **pooled** - the simple fava slope, ignoring inoculation.
* **adjusted** - the fava slope after also accounting for the other design factor (inoculation in
  Part 1; water in Part 2).

```{r libs}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)
library(emmeans)
library(car)
source("../fig_style.R")

inter <- readRDS("../wheat_audited.rds") %>% filter(Poly == "Inter")
stopifnot(nrow(inter) == 30, all(table(inter$Inoc, inter$Water) == 5),
          identical(levels(inter$Inoc), c("Inoc", "Strl")), all(inter$Num_fava == 1),
          all(inter$berry_alloc > 0 & inter$berry_alloc < 1))

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3)))

resp_lab <- c(alloc = "Berry allocation\n(proportion of wheat NPP)",
              bio   = "Wheat biomass\n(g per pot)")

fit_resp <- function(resp, rhs, data = inter) {
  if (resp == "alloc") glmmTMB(as.formula(paste("berry_alloc ~", rhs)), family = beta_family(), data = data)
  else                 lm(as.formula(paste("log(W_NPP) ~", rhs)), data = data)
}
slopes <- function(m, by) {
  as.data.frame(test(emtrends(m, as.formula(paste("~", by)), var = "Fava_g")))
}
norm_cl <- function(d) {
  names(d)[names(d) %in% c("lower.CL", "asymp.LCL")] <- "lcl"
  names(d)[names(d) %in% c("upper.CL", "asymp.UCL")] <- "ucl"
  d
}
```

# Collinearity check

Why the design below carries two p-values per slope. Fava and inoculation are nearly the same
variable at Control and Moderate, and only decouple at Severe.

```{r collin}
inter %>% group_by(Water) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `r(fava, Inoc)`  = round(cor(Fava_g, Inoc == "Inoc"), 2),
            `r(fava, hyphal colonization)` = round(cor(Fava_g, hyphal), 2),
            `fava mean, Inoc (g)` = round(mean(Fava_g[Inoc == "Inoc"]), 1),
            `fava mean, Strl (g)` = round(mean(Fava_g[Inoc == "Strl"]), 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

At Control and Moderate, the adjusted slope has little independent fava variation to work with, so
its CI will be wide. That is a property of the design, not of the analysis.

# Part 1 - Full intercrop set, by water

Three water levels (columns), two responses (rows). Line = pooled simple fit within each water level
(n = 10 pots), ribbon = 95% CI. Filled points = inoculated, open = sterile.

```{r modelsA}
mA <- list(
  alloc = list(pooled = fit_resp("alloc", "Fava_g * Water"),
               adj    = fit_resp("alloc", "Fava_g * Water + Inoc")),
  bio   = list(pooled = fit_resp("bio",   "Fava_g * Water"),
               adj    = fit_resp("bio",   "Fava_g * Water + Inoc"))
)

slopeA <- imap_dfr(mA, function(ms, r) {
  bind_rows(slopes(ms$pooled, "Water") %>% mutate(kind = "pooled"),
            slopes(ms$adj,    "Water") %>% mutate(kind = "adjusted")) %>% mutate(resp = r)
})
slopeA %>% transmute(resp, Water, kind, slope = round(Fava_g.trend, 3), SE = round(SE, 3),
                     p = signif(p.value, 3)) %>%
  arrange(resp, Water, kind) %>% knitr::kable()
```

```{r figA, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
grid <- seq(0.5, 10, length.out = 100)
rng  <- inter %>% group_by(Water) %>% summarise(lo = min(Fava_g), hi = max(Fava_g))

linesA <- imap_dfr(mA, function(ms, r) {
  emmeans(ms$pooled, ~ Fava_g * Water, at = list(Fava_g = grid), type = "response") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>% norm_cl() %>% mutate(resp = r)
}) %>% left_join(rng, by = "Water") %>% filter(Fava_g >= lo, Fava_g <= hi)

ptsA <- inter %>% transmute(Water, Inoc, Fava_g, alloc = berry_alloc, bio = W_NPP) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(alloc, bio), names_to = "resp", values_to = "y")

annA <- slopeA %>%
  select(resp, Water, kind, p.value) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = kind, values_from = p.value) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("slope ", fmt_p(pooled), " (pooled)\n",
                        "slope ", fmt_p(adjusted), " (adj. for Inoc)"))

relevel_resp <- function(d) mutate(d, resp = factor(resp, names(resp_lab), resp_lab))
linesA <- relevel_resp(linesA); ptsA <- relevel_resp(ptsA); annA <- relevel_resp(annA)

blue <- pal_poly[["Inter"]]
figA <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = linesA, aes(Fava_g, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), fill = blue, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = linesA, aes(Fava_g, response), color = blue, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = ptsA, aes(Fava_g, y, fill = Inoc), shape = 21, color = blue, size = 3, stroke = 1) +
  geom_text(data = annA, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label), hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.2,
            size = 3, color = "grey25", lineheight = 0.95) +
  facet_grid(resp ~ Water, scales = "free_y", switch = "y",
             labeller = labeller(Water = water_lab)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Inoc = blue, Strl = "white"), labels = inoc_lab) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.32))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2.5, 5, 7.5)) +
  labs(x = "Fava biomass (g per pot)", y = NULL,
       title = "Wheat allocation and biomass against fava biomass, wheat/ fava intercrop",
       subtitle = "Per pot, n = 10 per panel. Line = pooled fit with 95% CI; filled = inoculated, open = sterile.") +
  theme_ms(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey93", linewidth = 0.3),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey30"))
figA
ggsave("figures/Fig_FavaExplanatory_ByWater.pdf", figA, width = 11, height = 7)
ggsave("figures/Fig_FavaExplanatory_ByWater.png", figA, width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

# Part 2 - Split by inoculation (Inter-Inoc and Inter-Strl, n = 15 each)

With only 5 pots per Inoc x Water cell, per-cell slopes would be unreliable, so slopes are
estimated **within each inoculation treatment** (n = 15) and the three water levels are shown as
point shapes. Within each treatment fava varies with water (in Strl it falls from about 8.5 g at
Control to 4.1 g at Severe), so fava and water are partly confounded there.

* **pooled** p: `y ~ Fava * Inoc` - the simple fava slope within each inoculation treatment.
* **adjusted** p: `y ~ Fava * Inoc + Water` - the fava slope after accounting for water, assuming
  the slope does not differ by water (checked below). Fitted once on all 30 pots.

```{r modelsB}
mB <- list(
  alloc = list(pooled = fit_resp("alloc", "Fava_g * Inoc"),
               adj    = fit_resp("alloc", "Fava_g * Inoc + Water"),
               full   = fit_resp("alloc", "Fava_g * Inoc + Water + Fava_g:Water")),
  bio   = list(pooled = fit_resp("bio",   "Fava_g * Inoc"),
               adj    = fit_resp("bio",   "Fava_g * Inoc + Water"),
               full   = fit_resp("bio",   "Fava_g * Inoc + Water + Fava_g:Water"))
)

slopeB <- imap_dfr(mB, function(ms, r) {
  bind_rows(slopes(ms$pooled, "Inoc") %>% mutate(kind = "pooled"),
            slopes(ms$adj,    "Inoc") %>% mutate(kind = "adjusted")) %>% mutate(resp = r)
})
slopeB %>% transmute(resp, Inoc, kind, slope = round(Fava_g.trend, 3), SE = round(SE, 3),
                     p = signif(p.value, 3)) %>%
  arrange(resp, Inoc, kind) %>% knitr::kable()
```

Check on the assumption that the fava slope is the same at every water level (Fava x Water term in
the adjusted model; a small p would mean the additive-water model is too simple):

```{r checkB}
chkB <- imap_dfr(mB, function(ms, r) {
  a <- car::Anova(ms$full, type = 2)
  pcol <- grep("^Pr\\(", colnames(a), value = TRUE)[1]
  tibble(resp = r, p_Fava_x_Water = signif(a["Fava_g:Water", pcol], 3))
})
knitr::kable(chkB)
```

**Reading the check.** For allocation the Fava x Water term is clearly non-zero
(p = `r signif(chkB$p_Fava_x_Water[chkB$resp == "alloc"], 2)`): the fava slope is not the same at every
water level (Part 1 shows why: it is steep at Severe and flat at Control and Moderate). The
water-adjusted allocation slopes in Part 2 are therefore an *average* across water levels and should
not be read as a single clean effect; the by-water slopes in Part 1 describe allocation better. For
biomass the term is not distinguishable from zero (p = `r signif(chkB$p_Fava_x_Water[chkB$resp == "bio"], 2)`),
so the additive-water model is adequate there.

```{r figB, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=7}
rngB <- inter %>% group_by(Inoc) %>% summarise(lo = min(Fava_g), hi = max(Fava_g))

linesB <- imap_dfr(mB, function(ms, r) {
  emmeans(ms$pooled, ~ Fava_g * Inoc, at = list(Fava_g = grid), type = "response") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>% norm_cl() %>% mutate(resp = r)
}) %>% left_join(rngB, by = "Inoc") %>% filter(Fava_g >= lo, Fava_g <= hi)

ptsB <- inter %>% transmute(Water, Inoc, Fava_g, alloc = berry_alloc, bio = W_NPP) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(alloc, bio), names_to = "resp", values_to = "y")

annB <- slopeB %>%
  select(resp, Inoc, kind, p.value) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = kind, values_from = p.value) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("slope ", fmt_p(pooled), " (pooled)\n",
                        "slope ", fmt_p(adjusted), " (adj. for water)"))

linesB <- relevel_resp(linesB); ptsB <- relevel_resp(ptsB); annB <- relevel_resp(annB)
inoc_panel <- c(Inoc = "Inter - inoculated", Strl = "Inter - sterile")

figB <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = linesB, aes(Fava_g, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), fill = blue, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = linesB, aes(Fava_g, response), color = blue, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = ptsB, aes(Fava_g, y, shape = Water, fill = Inoc), color = blue, size = 3, stroke = 1) +
  geom_text(data = annB, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label), hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.2,
            size = 3, color = "grey25", lineheight = 0.95) +
  facet_grid(resp ~ Inoc, scales = "free", switch = "y",
             labeller = labeller(Inoc = inoc_panel)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Control = 21, Moderate = 24, Severe = 22), labels = water_lab) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Inoc = blue, Strl = "white"), guide = "none") +
  guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "grey60", color = "grey30"))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.32))) +
  labs(x = "Fava biomass (g per pot)", y = NULL,
       title = "Fava as an explanatory variable within each inoculation treatment",
       subtitle = "Per pot, n = 15 per panel (x-axes differ by panel). Line = pooled fit with 95% CI; shape = water level.") +
  theme_ms(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey93", linewidth = 0.3),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey30"))
figB
ggsave("figures/Fig_FavaExplanatory_ByInoc.pdf", figB, width = 9.5, height = 7)
ggsave("figures/Fig_FavaExplanatory_ByInoc.png", figB, width = 9.5, height = 7, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```
